title: Pair sum
prompt: Given an array of safe integers and a safe-integer target, return indices [i,j] with i < j whose values sum to target. Scan j left to right and choose the earliest stored i for that complement. Return null (Python None) if no pair exists. Do not mutate input.
solution: Store the first index of each value in a map; do not overwrite it on duplicates. Before inserting, check for target minus the current value and return the first match. This avoids index reuse and preserves the specified tie rule. Expected O(n) time, O(n) space.
edgeCases: Empty and single-item arrays return null.
Duplicate values may form a pair, but an index cannot be reused.
Negative values and zero are allowed.

title: Balanced brackets
prompt: Given a string containing only ()[]{}, return whether brackets match and nest correctly. The empty string is balanced.
solution: Push opening brackets onto a stack. For each closing bracket, pop and compare its matching opener. Reject mismatches or an empty stack. At the end the stack must be empty. O(n) time and O(n) auxiliary space.
edgeCases: Empty input is true.
A closing bracket without an opener is false.
Leftover openers and crossed nesting are false.

title: Merge intervals
prompt: Given unsorted inclusive integer intervals [start,end] where start <= end, merge overlapping intervals, including touching endpoints. Return intervals sorted by start without mutating the input.
solution: Copy and sort intervals by start. Extend the most recent merged interval when its end reaches the next start; otherwise append a new interval. Time is O(n log n).
edgeCases: Empty input returns an empty list.
Nested and identical intervals collapse.
[1,2] and [2,3] merge; [1,2] and [3,4] do not.

title: Delivery batches
prompt: Given non-negative integer item counts and a positive integer capacity, return the number of separate batches required. Each count belongs to one customer; never mix customers in one batch. Sum the ceiling of count/capacity.
edgeCases: Zero items require zero batches.
An exact multiple needs no partial batch.
solution: For each count, add floor(count/capacity) and one when there is a nonzero remainder. Sum independently. O(n) time and O(1) extra space.

title: First seen IDs
prompt: Given case-sensitive ASCII ID strings, return each distinct ID once in first-seen order. Preserve empty strings and do not mutate input.
edgeCases: All duplicates produce one ID.
"A" and "a" are distinct.
solution: Maintain a set of seen IDs and an output list. Append and mark only unseen IDs. Expected O(n) time; O(k) space for k distinct IDs.

title: Run labels
prompt: For a string of ASCII letters, return contiguous runs as [character,count] pairs. Uppercase and lowercase differ; do not merge separated runs.
edgeCases: A single letter has count 1.
Repeated runs of the same letter remain separate.
solution: Walk once, extending the current run when the next character matches, otherwise start a new run. O(n) time, O(r) output space.

title: Last unique character
prompt: Given an ASCII string, return the greatest zero-based index of a character occurring exactly once, or -1 when no such character exists. Spaces and letter case matter.
edgeCases: Empty input returns -1.
A single space is a unique character.
solution: Count all characters, then scan indices from right to left and return the first with frequency one. O(n) time; O(alphabet) space.

title: Window maxima sum
prompt: Given safe integers and an integer k with 1 <= k <= array length, return the greatest sum of a contiguous window of length k. The array is nonempty; do not mutate it.
edgeCases: All-negative inputs must not default to zero.
k equal to array length has exactly one window.
solution: Sum the first k values; slide by subtracting the departing value and adding the entering value. Initialize the maximum with the first window, not zero. O(n) time, O(1) space.

title: Missing attendance day
prompt: Given strictly increasing positive integer days and a positive limit, return the smallest missing day in 1..limit, or limit+1 if all days occur. Every provided day is <= limit.
edgeCases: A missing first day returns 1.
Fully present days return limit+1.
solution: Binary-search the first index i with days[i] != i+1. If none exists, the answer is length+1. Strict increase makes the mismatch predicate monotone. O(log n) time, O(1) space.

title: Peak room demand
prompt: Given half-open time bookings [start,end) with integer start < end, return the maximum simultaneous room demand. A booking ending at time t frees its room before a booking starting at t.
edgeCases: Empty input returns zero.
Simultaneous arrivals all count; departures at that time happen first.
solution: Create +1 arrival and -1 departure events, sort by time then delta (departures first), and track the maximum running count. O(n log n) time; O(n) space.

title: Smallest budget prefix
prompt: Given non-negative integer daily costs and a non-negative budget, return the longest prefix length with sum <= budget. A zero-cost day can extend the prefix. Do not mutate input.
edgeCases: Empty input returns zero.
The first cost exceeding budget returns zero.
solution: Accumulate non-negative costs until adding the next would exceed budget; return that index, or the full length. O(n) time, O(1) space. With precomputed prefix sums and many budgets, binary search gives O(log n) per query.

title: Folder depth
prompt: Given an absolute slash-separated path containing ASCII folder names, . and .., return its canonical absolute path. Ignore empty and . components; .. removes a folder if one exists and never climbs above root. Folder names other than . and .. are literal.
edgeCases: Repeated slashes collapse.
A folder named ... is a literal folder.
solution: Split by slash and maintain a stack. Ignore empty/dot components, pop on dot-dot when possible, and push other names. Join under one leading slash. O(n) time and space.

title: Next warmer reading
prompt: For integer daily temperatures, return for each day the number of days until a strictly warmer reading, or 0 if none exists. Equal temperatures are not warmer.
edgeCases: Descending and constant readings produce zeros.
Negative temperatures are valid.
solution: Keep indices of unresolved days in a decreasing-temperature stack. When a warmer day arrives, pop cooler indices and fill their distances. Each index enters and exits once: O(n) time and space.

title: Largest garden patch
prompt: Given a rectangular grid of 0 and 1, return the size of the largest four-directionally connected group of 1 cells without mutating input. The grid may have no rows or no columns.
edgeCases: Diagonal neighbors are not connected.
An empty or all-zero grid returns zero.
solution: Use a visited set and BFS or DFS from each unvisited 1. Count only up/down/left/right neighbors in bounds. O(rows*columns) time and space; keep visited separate to preserve input.
reviewNotes: Authored for Prepto; contract, examples, edge cases and reference complexity checked together. Examples are illustrative, not execution results.

title: Workshop ordering
prompt: Given n workshops numbered 0..n-1 and unique dependency pairs [before,after], return the lexicographically smallest valid ordering, or [] if a cycle exists. Each pair uses valid workshop IDs; n may be zero.
edgeCases: Disconnected workshops still appear.
Self-dependencies are cycles.
solution: Build indegrees and outgoing edges. Repeatedly take the smallest zero-indegree ID from a min-heap, emitting it and decrementing neighbors. Fewer than n emitted IDs signals a cycle. O((n+edges) log n) time, O(n+edges) space.

title: Fewest stamps
prompt: Given distinct positive integer stamp values and a non-negative integer target, return the fewest stamps summing exactly to target, with unlimited copies of each value. Return -1 if impossible.
edgeCases: Target zero requires zero stamps, even with no values.
An empty value list cannot reach a positive target.
solution: Let dp[0]=0 and all other sums be unreachable. For each sum, try every value no greater than it and minimize dp[sum-value]+1. O(target*number of values) time, O(target) space. Greedy choice is not sufficient.

title: Nonadjacent shifts
prompt: Given non-negative integer rewards for ordered shifts, choose any subset with no adjacent indices and return the greatest total reward. Choosing no shifts is allowed; input is not mutated.
edgeCases: Empty input returns zero.
One shift returns its reward.
solution: Maintain the best totals through the previous one and two shifts. For each reward choose max(previous, two-back+reward). O(n) time, O(1) extra space.
reviewNotes: Authored for Prepto; contract, examples, edge cases and reference complexity checked together. Examples are illustrative, not execution results.

title: Shortest tag cover
prompt: Given an ASCII text and a required ASCII string, return the shortest substring containing every required character with its required multiplicity. Ties choose the earliest start. Return an empty string if required is empty or no cover exists. Comparisons are case-sensitive.
edgeCases: Repeated required characters need enough copies.
Extra text characters may be inside a cover.
solution: Count required multiplicities. Expand a right boundary until requirements are met, then shrink left while preserving coverage, recording only strictly shorter windows to keep earliest ties. O(text length+required length) time, O(alphabet) space.
